semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: There is no domain in the list that is exactly equivalent to 'hematological oncology,' which is a subfield combining aspects of hematology (the study of blood) and oncology (the study of cancer) focusing specifically on blood cancers.

parent_domains.justification: Hematology is a broader field that encompasses 'hematological oncology' as it deals with blood disorders, including cancers of the blood.
Oncology is another parent field of 'hematological oncology,' given that this domain specifically deals with cancers, including those of blood origin.

closest_parent_domain.justification: Within the context of 'hematological oncology,' which focuses on cancers of the blood, 'oncology' serves as the closest parent domain, as it specifically covers all types of cancer, including blood-origin cancers.

child_domains.justification: 'Immunotherapy in hematology' can be considered a child domain as it relates to treating blood-related cancers using immune-based therapies, falling under 'hematological oncology.'

closest_child_domain.justification: Of the potential child domains, 'immunotherapy in hematology' is most relevant to 'hematological oncology,' focusing specifically on immunotherapy applications within blood cancers.

sibling_domains.justification: As 'hematological oncology' shares the commonality of focusing on treatment aspects of blood diseases similar to 'immunotherapy in hematology,' both are specialized areas within the intersection of hematology and oncology.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: Given the specific focus on treating blood-related disorders or cancers, 'immunotherapy in hematology' stands as the closest sibling to 'hematological oncology.'

unrelated_domains.justification: Radiation oncology is a separate domain focused on the use of radiation to treat cancer and does not specifically relate to blood cancers.
Oncology imaging deals with the diagnostic imaging aspect and does not directly relate to blood oncology.
This domain focuses on supporting cancer patients and their well-being, which, while important, does not directly relate to the study or treatment of hematological cancers.
Chemoinformatics pertains to the use of informatics in chemical data, which does not directly overlap with hematological oncology.
The study and application of radiology are diagnostic imaging-oriented, which does not specifically intersect with hematological oncology's focus on blood cancers.
Focuses on cancers found typically in children which can include but are not limited to blood cancers.
